svg.text: Interactive Learning Tool — Identify the Parts of a Flower

g.text: Examine the flower illustration and the 10
numbered label slots pointing to each part.
Use the Word Bank below to identify which
label belongs in each numbered slot.
Click "Check Answer" to reveal the correct
placements. Use "Hint" if you need help.

svg.text: WORD BANK — Match each label to its correct numbered slot

g.text: Colorful, often fragrant leaf-like structures that attract pollinators.
They are the most conspicuous part of the flower.
The sticky, often feathery top surface of the pistil that receives
The slender, tube-like structure connecting the stigma to the ovary.
It elevates the stigma to catch pollen.
The swollen, hollow base of the pistil containing ovules.
After fertilization, it develops into the fruit.
The thickened upper part of the stem where all flower parts
are attached. It supports the entire flower structure.
The pollen-producing tip of the stamen. It contains
The thin, stalk-like structure that supports the anther,
positioning it for effective pollen release.
The male reproductive organ, consisting of the filament
and anther together. Flowers typically have multiple stamens.
The female reproductive organ, made up of the stigma,
style, and ovary. Most flowers have one central pistil.
Green, leaf-like structures below the petals that protect
the flower bud before it opens. Collectively called the calyx.
Tip: Remember — Stamens are male parts (anther + filament),
Pistil is the female part (stigma + style + ovary)
Summary: 4 Accessory Parts + 5 Male Parts + 6 Female Part Components
Male = Stamen (Anther + Filament) | Female = Pistil (Stigma + Style + Ovary) | Accessory = Petal + Sepal + Receptacle
Note: Receptacle is structural. Stamen & Pistil count as whole organs in addition to their sub-parts.
All label slots have been cleared.
Return to the diagram and try matching the labels again.
Use the Hint button if you need help getting started.
